title: Define Optimize Apply user journey + gating UX states (pass/fail/timeout/override) and acceptance criteria
creator: Aditya Rao
body:
## Problem
Optimize can propose configuration changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing) that improve cost/latency but can cause user-visible quality regressions. We are adding mandatory evaluation-based gating before any Optimize-driven change is applied. This ticket defines the end-to-end user journey and the required UX states (Console + API) so engineering can build deterministic behavior and Support can explain outcomes.

## Scope
- Define the Optimize Apply flow in Console and API.
- Define gating UX states and transitions:
  - PASS
  - FAIL
  - TIMEOUT / EVAL RUNNER UNAVAILABLE
  - OVERRIDE (request/approved/applied)
  - OBSERVE-ONLY (rollout stage where we run + show results but do not block)
- Define what the user sees (summary + details) and what’s written to audit logs.
- Define acceptance criteria for ENG implementation (policy enforcement, runner integration, UI).

Non-scope
- Threshold methodology (owned by Applied ML / Evals)
- Exact metrics taxonomy (separate doc; we only reference how to display)

## User personas
1) Self-serve engineer (Hosted API): wants fast apply, clear blocking reasons, actionable next steps.
2) Enterprise platform admin (Dedicated/Private): needs audit trail, override pathway, and clear roles/permissions.
3) Support/Oncall: needs consistent state machine + error messaging, and links to artifacts for debugging.

## Glossary
- "Optimization proposal": Optimize-generated change set (one or multiple deltas).
- "Gating run": eval-harness invocation for the target model + prompt set + suite selector + proposed config delta.
- "Gate decision": computed pass/fail/unknown (timeout/unavailable) based on thresholds.

## End-to-end journey (Console)
### Entry points
A) Optimize recommendation card ("Apply" CTA)
B) Route-level Optimize page (bulk actions may come later; out of scope for GA)

### High-level steps
1. User clicks Apply on a recommendation.
2. Console shows a confirmation modal with:
   - Summary of config deltas (e.g., quantization profile, max batch size, cache toggles)
   - Expected cost/latency impact (if available)
   - Required guardrails suites to run (read-only)
   - Time estimate and that apply is gated by quality checks
3. User confirms "Run checks & apply".
4. System creates an async gating run and shows progress.
5. System reaches a terminal state:
   - PASS -> Apply proceeds automatically (or prompts user to confirm apply, depending on tier/rollout stage)
   - FAIL -> Apply is blocked; user can view details and (if permitted) request override
   - TIMEOUT/UNAVAILABLE -> Behavior depends on tier/rollout stage; see state machine below

### Display requirements (what to show)
Always show:
- Overall decision badge: Passed / Failed / Timed out / Pending / Override applied
- Timestamp + run id
- Model identifier + model version
- Prompt set revision
- Suite(s) executed
- A short explanation sentence (user-facing)

When details are expanded:
- Per-metric table:
  - metric name
  - baseline vs candidate values
  - delta
  - threshold / allowed regression
  - sample size
  - confidence/CI indicator (if provided)
- Links:
  - View artifacts (eval report)
  - Copy run id
  - View audit log event id (enterprise)

## Required UX states + transitions
### 1) PENDING (gating run created)
- UI: spinner + "Running quality checks" with ETA range.
- API: apply request returns 202 Accepted with gating_run_id and status=pending.
- User actions: cancel run (optional; v1 can be disabled).

### 2) PASS
- Definition: gate decision = pass.
- UI:
  - Show "Passed" + highlight top-level metrics
  - Next step depends on enforcement stage:
    - Observe-only: show "Would apply" messaging but do not apply; provide "Apply anyway" disabled or hidden (align to rollout plan)
    - Soft-block: apply allowed but show warning and require explicit confirmation checkbox ("I understand…")
    - Hard-block: pass required and auto-apply proceeds
- API:
  - If Apply is synchronous after pass: respond 200 with apply_result=applied and gating summary
  - If apply is decoupled: respond 200 with gating=pass and apply_job_id

### 3) FAIL
- Definition: one or more required metrics breach thresholds with min sample size satisfied.
- UI:
  - Show "Failed" state + top 1-3 failure reasons (e.g., "Task success -1.8pp exceeds -1.0pp limit")
  - Provide "View details" and "Rerun checks" (rerun is allowed if inputs unchanged; see acceptance criteria)
  - Provide "Request override" ONLY if user has permission and tenant policy allows overrides
  - Provide link to "How to resolve" doc section (public docs later)
- API:
  - If hard-block enforced: respond 409 Conflict (or 412 Precondition Failed) with structured failure reasons + gating_run_id
  - If observe-only: respond 200 and include gating_result=fail but apply proceeds only if allowed by rollout stage (explicitly controlled)

### 4) TIMEOUT / EVAL RUNNER UNAVAILABLE (UNKNOWN)
Split into two user-facing categories:
A) Timeout: run started but exceeded time budget
B) Unavailable: runner errors/outage

UI:
- Badge: "Timed out" or "Checks unavailable"
- Copy: "We couldn’t complete quality checks in time. No changes were applied." (hard-block default)
- Provide "Retry" (with backoff messaging) and "Contact support" link.

Behavior by tenant tier (initial proposal; finalize with PM-844):
- Hosted/Self-serve: block apply on timeout/unavailable.
- Dedicated/Enterprise: default block, but allow override request if RBAC allows and policy enables.

API:
- Return 503 Service Unavailable for runner unavailable (include gating_run_id if created)
- Return 504 Gateway Timeout (include gating_run_id)
- In both cases, include whether config change was applied (should be false) and next-step hints (retry_after_seconds)

### 5) OVERRIDE
Override is a controlled path that must be explicit and auditable.

Sub-states:
- Override requested (pending approval)
- Override approved (ready to apply)
- Override denied
- Override applied

UI requirements:
- "Request override" opens a form:
  - Required free-text justification
  - Optional link to incident/customer escalation (internal only)
  - Acknowledge that quality checks failed / were unavailable
- After request:
  - Show "Override requested" badge
  - Show who will review (role/team) and expected SLA (best-effort)
- If approved:
  - Provide "Apply with override" CTA with final confirmation
- If denied:
  - Show reason and next steps (rerun/adjust prompt set/adjust thresholds if appropriate)

API requirements:
- Separate endpoint preferred:
  - POST /optimize/applies/{id}/override-request
  - POST /optimize/applies/{id}/override-apply
- Override apply must include:
  - override_justification
  - approver identity (server-filled)
  - reference gating_run_id

## Copy guidelines (draft)
- Avoid saying "Your model is worse"; say "Failed quality checks".
- Always state whether changes were applied.
- Provide actionable next step in every terminal state (view details, retry, request override, contact support).

## Acceptance criteria
### Console UX
1. For an Optimize recommendation, user can initiate "Run checks & apply".
2. Console shows gating status updates until terminal state.
3. Terminal states are visually distinct and match above definitions.
4. Details view includes: model+version, prompt set revision, suite list, per-metric table, run id, artifacts link.
5. Fail state shows top reasons + rerun option.
6. Timeout/unavailable state clearly states changes not applied and offers retry.
7. Override request UI exists behind feature flag and only appears if user has permission.

### API behavior
1. Apply endpoint returns a stable, documented state machine:
   - pending | pass | fail | timeout | unavailable | override_requested | override_applied (final naming TBD but must be consistent)
2. If gating is required and decision is fail/timeout/unavailable, system does not apply config changes (unless override applied).
3. API returns structured failure reasons for fail (metric, delta, threshold, sample_size).
4. API includes gating_run_id in all responses after gating is initiated.
5. Rerunning identical gating inputs should either:
   - reuse cached results OR
   - explicitly return that a cached run was used (needs coordination with ENG-3916).

### Auditability (must be compatible with audit event spec)
1. For every apply attempt, we emit an audit event including:
   - actor, tenant, route/model identifiers
   - config delta summary
   - gating decision + reasons
   - prompt set rev + suite + eval-harness version
   - override fields if applicable
2. Console surfaces audit event id for enterprise tenants.

### Rollout compatibility
1. UX supports observe-only stage (shows results but doesn’t block).
2. UX supports soft-block stage (warn + allow via explicit confirmation or override policy).
3. UX supports hard-block stage (pass required).

## Open questions
1) Do we want PASS to auto-apply immediately or require a final confirmation click after results are displayed? (My proposal: auto-apply for self-serve when pass; enterprise can be a tenant setting.)
2) For timeout/unavailable: do we distinguish between "runner down" vs "job backlog" in user-facing copy? (Proposal: keep user-facing copy simple; include detailed error in internal logs.)
3) What is the default rerun behavior if prompt set changes between recommendation creation and apply? (Proposal: always rerun; cached results invalid.)

## Notes for engineering handoff
- This ticket is intended to unblock ENG-3913 (enforcement) and ENG-3917 (UI panel). Please confirm final state names early to avoid breaking changes.

---
## Updates / comments
### 2025-01-16 (Kenji Nakamura)
Drafted state machine and initial copy guidelines. Flagging question on PASS auto-apply vs second confirmation; will align with Aditya + SRE on risk tradeoff.

### 2025-01-20 (Aditya Rao)
Added observe-only and soft-block behavior so rollout stages don’t require UX redesign. Please ensure API returns "was_applied" boolean explicitly in all terminal states.

### 2025-01-23 (Sean Gallagher)
SRE note: for runner partial outage we need deterministic behavior (block for self-serve). For enterprise we can allow override request but should rate-limit to avoid papering over outages.

### 2025-01-27 (Chloe Martin)
Console backend can support polling by gating_run_id and returning summary + artifact links. Need final naming for timeout vs unavailable error codes (align with platform error taxonomy).
next_steps: Kenji + Aditya: finalize PASS auto-apply behavior per tier and document in UX spec
Aditya: resolve open questions with PM-844 (policy defaults for timeout/unavailable and overrides)
Hand off final state names + acceptance criteria to ENG-3913/ENG-3917 owners
